sanskrit: jātakarmāṇi sarvāṇi kārayām āsa pārthivaḥ puṃvad vidhānayuktāni śikhaṇḍīti ca tāṃ viduḥ
english: The king had all the birth-rites duly performed as for a male child, complete with their proper ordinances; and they knew her as Śikhaṇḍin.

sanskrit: aham ekas tu cāreṇa vacanān nāradasya ca jñātavān devavākyena ambāyās tapasā tathā
english: I alone came to know the truth—through my spies, through the words of Nārada, through the speech of the gods, and through the austerities of Ambā.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca cakāra yatnaṃ drupadaḥ sarvasmin svajane mahat tato lekhyādiṣu tathā śilpeṣu ca paraṃ gatā iṣvastre caiva rājendra droṇaśiṣyo babhūva ha
english: Bhīṣma said: Drupada took the greatest pains over all that concerned his own child; and so, O lord of kings, that child attained excellence in writing and the other arts, and in the crafts, and in archery became a pupil of Droṇa.

sanskrit: tasya mātā mahārāja rājānaṃ varavarṇinī codayām āsa bhāryārthaṃ kanyāyāḥ putravat tadā
english: The fair-complexioned mother of that child, O great king, then urged the king to seek a wife for the maiden as though for a son.

sanskrit: tatas tāṃ pārṣato dṛṣṭvā kanyāṃ saṃprāptayauvanām striyaṃ matvā tadā cintāṃ prapede saha bhāryayā
english: Then the son of Pṛṣata, seeing that the maiden had reached her youth and knowing her to be a woman, fell into anxiety together with his wife.

sanskrit: drupada uvāca kanyā mameyaṃ saṃprāptā yauvanaṃ śokavardhinī mayā pracchāditā ceyaṃ vacanāc chūlapāṇinaḥ
english: Drupada said: This maiden of mine, who increases my sorrow, has come to her youth; and I have kept her concealed in obedience to the word of the trident-bearer.

sanskrit: na tan mithyā mahārājñi bhaviṣyati kathaṃ cana trailokyakartā kasmād dhi tan mṛṣā kartum arhati
english: That word, O great queen, can in no way prove false; for why should the maker of the three worlds make it untrue?

sanskrit: bhāryovāca yadi te rocate rājan vakṣyāmi śṛṇu me vacaḥ śrutvedānīṃ prapadyethāḥ svakāryaṃ pṛṣatātmaja
english: His wife said: If it please you, O king, I will speak; hear my words. Hearing them now, O son of Pṛṣata, you may set about your own affair.

sanskrit: kriyatām asya nṛpate vidhivad dārasaṃgrahaḥ satyaṃ bhavati tad vākyam iti me niścitā matiḥ
english: Let a wife be duly taken for this child, O king; my settled conviction is that the word of the god will come true.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tatas tau niścayaṃ kṛtvā tasmin kārye 'tha dampatī varayāṃ cakratuḥ kanyāṃ daśārṇādhipateḥ sutām
english: Bhīṣma said: Then the husband and wife, having made their decision in that matter, sought as bride the daughter of the lord of the Daśārṇas.

sanskrit: tato rājā drupado rājasiṃhaḥ; sarvān rājñaḥ kulataḥ saṃniśāmya dāśārṇakasya nṛpates tanūjāṃ; śikhaṇḍine varayām āsa dārān
english: Then King Drupada, that lion among kings, having reviewed all the kings by their lineage, sought as a wife for Śikhaṇḍin the daughter of the Daśārṇaka king.

sanskrit: hiraṇyavarmeti nṛpo yo 'sau dāśārṇakaḥ smṛtaḥ sa ca prādān mahīpālaḥ kanyāṃ tasmai śikhaṇḍine
english: The king known as Hiraṇyavarman, that Daśārṇaka, that protector of the earth, gave his daughter to that Śikhaṇḍin.

sanskrit: sa ca rājā daśārṇeṣu mahān āsīn mahīpatiḥ hiraṇyavarmā durdharṣo mahāseno mahāmanāḥ
english: And that king Hiraṇyavarman was a great lord of the earth among the Daśārṇas—unassailable, master of a mighty army, lofty of mind.

sanskrit: kṛte vivāhe tu tadā sā kanyā rājasattama yauvanaṃ samanuprāptā sā ca kanyā śikhaṇḍinī
english: When the marriage had been made, O best of kings, that maiden came to her youth, and the maiden Śikhaṇḍinī likewise.

sanskrit: kṛtadāraḥ śikhaṇḍī tu kāmpilyaṃ punar āgamat na ca sā veda tāṃ kanyāṃ kaṃ cit kālaṃ striyaṃ kila
english: Śikhaṇḍin, now wedded, returned again to Kāmpilya; and for some time that maiden did not learn that the other was a woman.

sanskrit: hiraṇyavarmaṇaḥ kanyā jñātvā tāṃ tu śikhaṇḍinīm dhātrīṇāṃ ca sakhīnāṃ ca vrīḍamānā nyavedayat kanyāṃ pañcālarājasya sutāṃ tāṃ vai śikhaṇḍinīm
english: But the daughter of Hiraṇyavarman, having found out that Śikhaṇḍinī was a woman, in shame reported to her nurses and her companions that the daughter of the Pāñcāla king, that Śikhaṇḍinī, was indeed a maiden.

sanskrit: tatas tā rājaśārdūla dhātryo dāśārṇikās tadā jagmur ārtiṃ parāṃ duḥkhāt preṣayām āsur eva ca
english: Then, O tiger among kings, those Daśārṇa nurses fell into the deepest distress out of grief, and sent word.

sanskrit: tato daśārṇādhipateḥ preṣyāḥ sarvaṃ nyavedayan vipralambhaṃ yathāvṛttaṃ sa ca cukrodha pārthivaḥ
english: Then the messengers reported the whole deceit, just as it had happened, to the lord of the Daśārṇas; and that king flew into a rage.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍy api mahārāja puṃvad rājakule tadā vijahāra mudā yuktaḥ strītvaṃ naivātirocayan
english: Śikhaṇḍin too, O great king, lived in the royal household after the manner of a man, full of joy, in no way relishing womanhood.

sanskrit: tataḥ katipayāhasya tac chrutvā bharatarṣabha hiraṇyavarmā rājendra roṣād ārtiṃ jagāma ha
english: Then after a few days, O bull of the Bharatas, hearing this, King Hiraṇyavarman, O lord of kings, was driven to anguish by his fury.

sanskrit: tato dāśārṇako rājā tīvrakopasamanvitaḥ dūtaṃ prasthāpayām āsa drupadasya niveśane
english: Then the Daśārṇaka king, filled with fierce wrath, dispatched a messenger to the dwelling of Drupada.

sanskrit: tato drupadam āsādya dūtaḥ kāñcanavarmaṇaḥ eka ekāntam utsārya raho vacanam abravīt
english: Then the messenger of Kāñcanavarman, coming to Drupada, drew him aside alone and spoke in secret these words.

sanskrit: daśārṇarājo rājaṃs tvām idaṃ vacanam abravīt abhiṣaṅgāt prakupito vipralabdhas tvayānagha
english: The Daśārṇa king, O sovereign, sends you these words, enraged at the affront, deceived by you, O blameless one:

sanskrit: avamanyase māṃ nṛpate nūnaṃ durmantritaṃ tava yan me kanyāṃ svakanyārthe mohād yācitavān asi
english: You hold me in contempt, O king—surely your counsel has been evil—in that out of folly you asked of me my daughter for the sake of your own daughter.

sanskrit: tasyādya vipralambhasya phalaṃ prāpnuhi durmate eṣa tvāṃ sajanāmātyam uddharāmi sthiro bhava
english: Receive now the fruit of that deceit, O fool. Stand firm—I shall root you out, together with your kinsmen and your ministers.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evam uktasya dūtena drupadasya tadā nṛpa corasyeva gṛhītasya na prāvartata bhāratī
english: Bhīṣma said: When Drupada was thus addressed by the messenger, O king, his speech failed him, as though he were a thief caught in the act.

sanskrit: sa yatnam akarot tīvraṃ saṃbandhair anusāntvanaiḥ dūtair madhurasaṃbhāṣair naitad astīti saṃdiśan
english: He made a strenuous effort, sending word through kinsmen with soothing assurances and through messengers of honeyed speech, declaring, "This is not so."

sanskrit: sa rājā bhūya evātha kṛtvā tattvata āgamam kanyeti pāñcālasutāṃ tvaramāṇo 'bhiniryayau
english: But that king, having once more learned the truth—that the child of the Pāñcāla was a maiden—set out in haste.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃpreṣayām āsa mitrāṇām amitaujasām duhitur vipralambhaṃ taṃ dhātrīṇāṃ vacanāt tadā
english: Then he sent word to his allies of measureless might of the deceit practised upon his daughter, on the testimony of the nurses.

sanskrit: tataḥ samudayaṃ kṛtvā balānāṃ rājasattamaḥ abhiyāne matiṃ cakre drupadaṃ prati bhārata
english: Then that best of kings, mustering his forces, resolved to march against Drupada, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃmantrayām āsa mitraiḥ saha mahīpatiḥ hiraṇyavarmā rājendra pāñcālyaṃ pārthivaṃ prati
english: Then King Hiraṇyavarman, O lord of kings, took counsel with his allies concerning the Pāñcāla sovereign.

sanskrit: tatra vai niścitaṃ teṣām abhūd rājñāṃ mahātmanām tathyaṃ ced bhavati hy etat kanyā rājañ śikhaṇḍinī baddhvā pāñcālarājānam ānayiṣyāmahe gṛhān
english: There this was resolved among those high-souled kings: "If, O king, it prove true that Śikhaṇḍinī is a maiden, we shall bind the Pāñcāla king and bring him to our homes;

sanskrit: anyaṃ rājānam ādhāya pāñcāleṣu nareśvaram ghātayiṣyāma nṛpatiṃ drupadaṃ saśikhaṇḍinam
english: and having set up another king, another lord of men, among the Pāñcālas, we shall put to death King Drupada together with Śikhaṇḍin."

sanskrit: sa tadā dūtam ājñāya punaḥ kṣattāram īśvaraḥ prāsthāpayat pārṣatāya hanmīti tvāṃ sthiro bhava
english: Then that lord again instructed a messenger, an envoy, and dispatched him to the son of Pṛṣata: "I shall slay you—stand firm!"

sanskrit: sa prakṛtyā ca vai bhīruḥ kilbiṣī ca narādhipaḥ bhayaṃ tīvram anuprāpto drupadaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ
english: And that lord of men, timid by nature and conscious of guilt, King Drupada, ruler of the earth, was seized with sharp dread.

sanskrit: visṛjya dūtaṃ dāśārṇaṃ drupadaḥ śokakarśitaḥ sametya bhāryāṃ rahite vākyam āha narādhipaḥ
english: Having dismissed the Daśārṇa messenger, Drupada, worn with grief, came to his wife in private and the king spoke these words.

sanskrit: bhayena mahatāviṣṭo hṛdi śokena cāhataḥ pāñcālarājo dayitāṃ mātaraṃ vai śikhaṇḍinaḥ
english: Possessed by great fear and stricken to the heart with sorrow, the Pāñcāla king said to the beloved mother of Śikhaṇḍin:

sanskrit: abhiyāsyati māṃ kopāt saṃbandhī sumahābalaḥ hiraṇyavarmā nṛpatiḥ karṣamāṇo varūthinīm
english: "My kinsman of mighty strength, King Hiraṇyavarman, will march against me in his wrath, dragging his host along.

sanskrit: kim idānīṃ kariṣyāmi mūḍhaḥ kanyām imāṃ prati śikhaṇḍī kila putras te kanyeti pariśaṅkitaḥ
english: What shall I now do, bewildered, concerning this maiden? Śikhaṇḍin, said to be your son, is suspected to be a maiden.

sanskrit: iti niścitya tattvena samitraḥ sabalānugaḥ vañcito 'smīti manvāno māṃ kiloddhartum icchati
english: Having ascertained this as the truth, with his allies and his host of followers, deeming himself deceived, he wishes, it seems, to uproot me.

sanskrit: kim atra tathyaṃ suśroṇi kiṃ mithyā brūhi śobhane śrutvā tvattaḥ śubhe vākyaṃ saṃvidhāsyāmy ahaṃ tathā
english: What in this is true, O fair-hipped one, and what is false? Tell me, O lovely one. Having heard your word, O auspicious one, I shall act accordingly.

sanskrit: ahaṃ hi saṃśayaṃ prāpto bālā ceyaṃ śikhaṇḍinī tvaṃ ca rājñi mahat kṛcchraṃ saṃprāptā varavarṇini
english: For I am fallen into doubt, and this Śikhaṇḍinī is but a child; and you too, O queen, fair of hue, have come into great straits.

sanskrit: sā tvaṃ sarvavimokṣāya tattvam ākhyāhi pṛcchataḥ tathā vidadhyāṃ suśroṇi kṛtyasyāsya śucismite śikhaṇḍini ca mā bhais tvaṃ vidhāsye tatra tattvataḥ
english: Tell me then the truth, as I ask, for our deliverance from all this, so that I may take measures in this matter, O fair-hipped, bright-smiling one; and do not fear for Śikhaṇḍin—I shall surely make provision there.

sanskrit: kriyayāhaṃ varārohe vañcitaḥ putradharmataḥ mayā dāśārṇako rājā vañcitaś ca mahīpatiḥ tad ācakṣva mahābhāge vidhāsye tatra yad dhitam
english: By my own deed, O lovely one, I have been deceived as to the office of a son; and the Daśārṇaka king too, that lord of the earth, has been deceived by me. So tell me, O blessed one, and I shall do in this what is best.

sanskrit: jānatāpi narendreṇa khyāpanārthaṃ parasya vai prakāśaṃ coditā devī pratyuvāca mahīpatim
english: Though the king knew the truth, he urged it openly so as to make it plain to the other; and the queen replied to the lord of the earth.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tataḥ śikhaṇḍino mātā yathātattvaṃ narādhipa ācacakṣe mahābāho bhartre kanyāṃ śikhaṇḍinīm
english: Bhīṣma said: Then the mother of Śikhaṇḍin, O ruler of men, O mighty-armed one, declared the truth to her husband—that Śikhaṇḍinī was a maiden:

sanskrit: aputrayā mayā rājan sapatnīnāṃ bhayād idam kanyā śikhaṇḍinī jātā puruṣo vai niveditaḥ
english: "Being without a son, O king, and through fear of my co-wives, I declared this maiden Śikhaṇḍinī, when she was born, to be a male.

sanskrit: tvayā caiva naraśreṣṭha tan me prītyānumoditam putrakarma kṛtaṃ caiva kanyāyāḥ pārthivarṣabha bhāryā coḍhā tvayā rājan daśārṇādhipateḥ sutā
english: And you, O best of men, approved this of me out of love; the rites of a son were performed for the maiden, O bull among kings, and a wife was taken for her by you, O king—the daughter of the lord of the Daśārṇas.

sanskrit: tvayā ca prāg abhihitaṃ devavākyārthadarśanāt kanyā bhūtvā pumān bhāvīty evaṃ caitad upekṣitam
english: And it was you who said before, considering the meaning of the god's word, 'Having been a maiden, she shall become a man'—and so this was let be.

sanskrit: etac chrutvā drupado yajñasenaḥ; sarvaṃ tattvaṃ mantravidbhyo nivedya mantraṃ rājā mantrayām āsa rājan; yad yad yuktaṃ rakṣaṇe vai prajānām
english: Hearing this, Drupada Yajñasena, O king, laid the whole truth before his counsellors versed in deliberation, and took counsel as to whatever was fitting for the protection of his people.

sanskrit: saṃbandhakaṃ caiva samarthya tasmin; dāśārṇake vai nṛpatau narendra svayaṃ kṛtvā vipralambhaṃ yathāvan; mantraikāgro niścayaṃ vai jagāma
english: And having weighed the kinship-bond with that Daśārṇaka king, O lord of men—since he had himself wrought the deceit as it had happened—intent upon his counsel, he came to a resolve.

sanskrit: svabhāvaguptaṃ nagaram āpatkāle tu bhārata gopayām āsa rājendra sarvataḥ samalaṃkṛtam
english: In that time of peril, O Bhārata, the king secured on every side his city—naturally well guarded and fully arrayed for defence, O lord of kings.

sanskrit: ārtiṃ ca paramāṃ rājā jagāma saha bhāryayā daśārṇapatinā sārdhaṃ virodhe bharatarṣabha
english: And the king, together with his wife, fell into the deepest distress over the strife with the lord of the Daśārṇas, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: kathaṃ saṃbandhinā sārdhaṃ na me syād vigraho mahān iti saṃcintya manasā daivatāny arcayat tadā
english: "How may there be no great quarrel between me and my kinsman?"—thus reflecting in his mind, he then worshipped the gods.

sanskrit: taṃ tu dṛṣṭvā tadā rājan devī devaparaṃ tathā arcāṃ prayuñjānam atho bhāryā vacanam abravīt
english: Seeing him then, O king, devoted to the gods and engaged in worship, the queen, his wife, spoke these words.

sanskrit: devānāṃ pratipattiś ca satyā sādhumatā sadā sā tu duḥkhārṇavaṃ prāpya naḥ syād arcayatāṃ bhṛśam
english: "Reverence for the gods is ever true and esteemed by the good; and it may avail us, who have fallen into an ocean of grief, if we worship them earnestly.

sanskrit: daivatāni ca sarvāṇi pūjyantāṃ bhūridakṣiṇaiḥ agnayaś cāpi hūyantāṃ dāśārṇapratiṣedhane
english: Let all the gods be honoured with abundant gifts, and let the sacred fires too be fed with oblations, for the turning back of the Daśārṇa.

sanskrit: ayuddhena nivṛttiṃ ca manasā cintayābhibho devatānāṃ prasādena sarvam etad bhaviṣyati
english: And ponder in your mind, O lord, his turning back without battle; by the grace of the gods all this shall come to pass.

sanskrit: mantribhir mantritaṃ sārdhaṃ tvayā yat pṛthulocana purasyāsyāvināśāya tac ca rājaṃs tathā kuru
english: And what has been deliberated by your ministers together with you, O wide-eyed one, for the saving of this city, O king, that too carry out accordingly.

sanskrit: daivaṃ hi mānuṣopetaṃ bhṛśaṃ sidhyati pārthiva parasparavirodhāt tu nānayoḥ siddhir asti vai
english: For the divine, joined with human effort, succeeds full well, O king; but from the mutual opposition of the two there is no success at all."

sanskrit: tasmād vidhāya nagare vidhānaṃ sacivaiḥ saha arcayasva yathākāmaṃ daivatāni viśāṃ pate
english: "Therefore, having made arrangements in the city together with your counsellors, worship the gods to your heart's content, O lord of peoples."

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃbhāṣamāṇau tau dṛṣṭvā śokaparāyaṇau śikhaṇḍinī tadā kanyā vrīḍiteva manasvinī
english: Seeing the two thus conversing, given over wholly to grief, the maiden Śikhaṇḍinī, high-minded, was as if overcome with shame.

sanskrit: tataḥ sā cintayām āsa matkṛte duḥkhitāv ubhau imāv iti tataś cakre matiṃ prāṇavināśane
english: Then she thought, "It is on my account that these two are grieving"; and thereupon she set her mind upon ending her life.

sanskrit: evaṃ sā niścayaṃ kṛtvā bhṛśaṃ śokaparāyaṇā jagāma bhavanaṃ tyaktvā gahanaṃ nirjanaṃ vanam
english: Having thus made her resolve, utterly given over to grief, she left the palace and went to a dense, deserted forest,

sanskrit: yakṣeṇarddhimatā rājan sthūṇākarṇena pālitam tadbhayād eva ca jano visarjayati tad vanam
english: guarded, O king, by a yakṣa rich in power, Sthūṇākarṇa; and for very dread of him men shun that forest.

sanskrit: tatra sthūṇasya bhavanaṃ sudhāmṛttikalepanam lājollāpikadhūmāḍhyam uccaprākāratoraṇam
english: There stood the dwelling of Sthūṇa, plastered with lime and clay, rich with the smoke of parched grain and frankincense, with high ramparts and gateway-arches.

sanskrit: tat praviśya śikhaṇḍī sā drupadasyātmajā nṛpa anaśnatī bahutithaṃ śarīram upaśoṣayat
english: Entering it, Śikhaṇḍin, the child of Drupada, O king, took no food for many days and wasted away her body.

sanskrit: darśayām āsa tāṃ yakṣaḥ sthūṇo madhvakṣasaṃyutaḥ kimartho 'yaṃ tavārambhaḥ kariṣye brūhi māciram
english: The yakṣa Sthūṇa, gracious of eye, showed himself to her: "For what purpose is this endeavour of yours? I shall accomplish it—tell me, do not delay."

sanskrit: aśakyam iti sā yakṣaṃ punaḥ punar uvāca ha kariṣyāmīti caināṃ sa pratyuvācātha guhyakaḥ
english: "It cannot be done," she said to the yakṣa again and again; and the guhyaka answered her, "I shall do it."

sanskrit: dhaneśvarasyānucaro varado 'smi nṛpātmaje adeyam api dāsyāmi brūhi yat te vivakṣitam
english: "I am a follower of the lord of wealth and a bestower of boons, O daughter of a king; even what may not be given, I shall give. Speak what you wish to ask."

sanskrit: tataḥ śikhaṇḍī tat sarvam akhilena nyavedayat tasmai yakṣapradhānāya sthūṇākarṇāya bhārata
english: Then Śikhaṇḍin laid the whole matter, entire, before that chief of yakṣas, Sthūṇākarṇa, O Bhārata:

sanskrit: āpanno me pitā yakṣa nacirād vinaśiṣyati abhiyāsyati saṃkruddho daśārṇādhipatir hi tam
english: "My father is in peril, O yakṣa; before long he will perish, for the lord of the Daśārṇas in his wrath will march against him—

sanskrit: mahābalo mahotsāhaḥ sa hemakavaco nṛpaḥ tasmād rakṣasva māṃ yakṣa pitaraṃ mātaraṃ ca me
english: a king of great might and great vigour, clad in golden armour. Therefore save me, O yakṣa, and my father and my mother.

sanskrit: pratijñāto hi bhavatā duḥkhapratinayo mama bhaveyaṃ puruṣo yakṣa tvatprasādād aninditaḥ
english: For you have promised to take away my sorrow. Let me become a man, O yakṣa, blameless, by your grace.

sanskrit: yāvad eva sa rājā vai nopayāti puraṃ mama tāvad eva mahāyakṣa prasādaṃ kuru guhyaka
english: Only until that king draws near my city—until then, O great yakṣa, O guhyaka, show me your favour."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca śikhaṇḍivākyaṃ śrutvātha sa yakṣo bharatarṣabha provāca manasā cintya daivenopanipīḍitaḥ bhavitavyaṃ tathā tad dhi mama duḥkhāya kaurava
english: Bhīṣma said: Hearing the words of Śikhaṇḍin, O bull of the Bharatas, that yakṣa, pressed by fate, reflected in his mind and spoke—for it was destined to be, and to my own sorrow, O Kaurava:

sanskrit: bhadre kāmaṃ kariṣyāmi samayaṃ tu nibodha me kiṃ cit kālāntaraṃ dāsye puṃliṅgaṃ svam idaṃ tava āgantavyaṃ tvayā kāle satyam etad bravīmi te
english: "Gentle one, I shall do your will, but mark my condition. For a certain space of time I shall give you this my own manhood; but you must return at the appointed time. This I tell you truly.

sanskrit: prabhuḥ saṃkalpasiddho 'smi kāmarūpī vihaṃgamaḥ matprasādāt puraṃ caiva trāhi bandhūṃś ca kevalān
english: I am a lord whose will is fulfilled, a sky-ranger who can take any form at pleasure. By my grace save your city and all your kinsmen entire.

sanskrit: strīliṅgaṃ dhārayiṣyāmi tvadīyaṃ pārthivātmaje satyaṃ me pratijānīhi kariṣyāmi priyaṃ tava
english: I shall bear your womanhood, O daughter of a king. Promise me truly, and I shall do you this kindness."

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍy uvāca pratidāsyāmi bhagavaṃl liṅgaṃ punar idaṃ tava kiṃ cit kālāntaraṃ strītvaṃ dhārayasva niśācara
english: Śikhaṇḍin said: "I shall give back to you this manhood again, O blessed one; for a certain space of time bear my womanhood, O night-ranger.
